parts.latex: Which of the following could be the graph of $y = -2x + 2$?

solutions.latex:
For $y=-2x+2$ the gradient is $-2$, so the line slopes downwards from left to right.

The $y$-intercept is found by putting $x=0$:
$$y=2$$
The $x$-intercept is found by putting $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned} 0&=-2x+2\\ x&=1 \end{aligned}$$
So the line has negative gradient, a positive $y$-intercept and a positive $x$-intercept.

Only option A has all three features: B has a negative $y$-intercept and C and D have positive gradient.

So the answer is option A.

parts.latex:
Suppose $y = -1 - 2x$.

When the value of $x$ increases by 5, the value of $y$ decreases by

solutions.latex:
The gradient of $y=-1-2x$ is $-2$, so $y$ changes by $-2$ for each increase of $1$ in $x$.

When $x$ increases by $5$:
$$\begin{aligned} \Delta y &= -2\times 5 \\ &= -10 \end{aligned}$$
So $y$ decreases by $10$.

$$\therefore\ y \text{ decreases by } 10$$

parts.latex:
Chloe has saved to buy a new phone that costs \$1018.

Her parents gave her \$100 and she saved \$34 per week until she had enough money to buy the phone.

The equation $y = mx + c$ models the amount of money that Chloe has.

Which row shows the correct values for $m, x$ and $c$?

solutions.latex:
In $y = mx + c$, $c$ is the starting amount and $m$ is the amount added each week, so $x$ is the number of weeks.

The starting amount is $c = 100$ and the weekly saving is $m = 34$.

For the phone, $y = 1018$, so
$$\begin{aligned} 1018 &= 34x + 100 \\ 34x &= 918 \\ x &= 27 \end{aligned}$$
So $m = 34$, $x = 27$ and $c = 100$, which is option D.

6697.stem: The volume ($V$ litres) of water in a tank as it is being drained over time ($t$) minutes can be modelled by the equation $V = 360 - 12t$.

parts.latex: At what rate is the tank draining?
What is the initial volume of the tank?
After how many minutes will the tank have half the initial volume of water?

solutions.latex:
The rate of draining is the gradient of $V = 360 - 12t$, which is $-12$.

Hence the tank drains at $12$ L/min.

The initial volume is the $V$-intercept, found by putting $t = 0$.
$$V = 360 - 12(0) = 360$$
Hence the initial volume is $360$ litres.

Half the initial volume is $\dfrac{360}{2} = 180$ litres, so put $V = 180$.
$$\begin{aligned} 360 - 12t &= 180 \\ 12t &= 180 \\ t &= 15 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the tank has half its initial volume after } 15 \text{ minutes}$$
criteria: Shows understanding that $V = 180$, or equivalent merit

7354.stem: The volume ($V$) (litres) of water in a tank as it is being drained over time ($t$) minutes can be modelled by the equation: $V = 250 - 10t$.

parts.latex: At what rate is the tank draining?
After how many minutes will the tank have half the initial volume of water?

solutions.latex:
In $V=250-10t$, the volume decreases by $10$ litres for each minute (the gradient is $-10$).
$$\therefore\ \text{the tank drains at } 10 \text{ litres per minute}$$

The initial volume is $V=250$ (when $t=0$), so half of it is $125$ litres.
$$\begin{aligned} 250-10t &= 125 \\ 10t &= 125 \\ t &= 12.5 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{after } 12.5 \text{ minutes}$$

figures.cap: straight line with y-intercept 15 and x-intercept 5

parts.latex:
Which equation describes this straight-line graph?

\exfigure{264_q6_1}

solutions.latex:
Read from the graph: the $y$-intercept is $15$ and the $x$-intercept is $5$.

The gradient is
$$m = \dfrac{0 - 15}{5 - 0} = -3$$
Using $y = mx + b$ with $b = 15$:
$$y = -3x + 15$$
This matches option A.

figures.cap: line through (1,0) and (3,1)

solutions.latex:
The gradient of a line through $(x_1,y_1)$ and $(x_2,y_2)$ is $m=\dfrac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}$.
$$\begin{aligned} m &= \dfrac{1-0}{3-1} \\ &= \dfrac{1}{2} \\ &= 0.5 \end{aligned}$$
The line slopes upwards, so the gradient is positive, which rules out A and B. Hence the gradient is $0.5$, option D.
